- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and overshoot; reduce forecast slope slightly.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to avoid missing downside.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap upward momentum after peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00/0.25), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-7 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from model in first 5-7 days of forecast horizon, apply “early correction” by shifting forecast downward if sentiment is bearish or upward if bullish.
- Model tends to lag in capturing sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 1-2 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid linear extrapolation; introduce slight curvature or smoothing to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven reversals.
